description: Task 4.4 Extensive Testing (CRITICAL). Substantially raise test coverage across xplainit-core and the CLI/dashboard with unit, integration, edge-case, hand-rolled property-style, and in-process load tests. proptest/quickcheck and cargo-fuzz/tarpaulin are UNAVAILABLE offline, so property testing is hand-rolled and coverage is reported qualitatively (tool-unavailable). Every new test must fail if the code under test is reverted. NOTE: FEAT-004 uses type 'test'; if the repo's commit lint only allows feat/chore/docs/fix/refactor, commit it as 'test:'-style message but the task type here documents intent.
steps: Inventory current coverage qualitatively: list modules in xplainit-core/src with thin or no tests (e.g. explainer.rs, error_explainer.rs, advanced_filter.rs, ast.rs, async_tracker.rs, formatter.rs, sink.rs, event_store.rs) and the security/error-recovery/redaction code added in FEAT-001/002. Do NOT run cargo tarpaulin (unavailable); state coverage is measured qualitatively.

Add unit + edge-case tests for under-tested core modules: empty inputs, deeply nested/large structures, malformed events, boundary depths (0 and max_depth), unicode/long strings, and error branches. Focus on real behavior assertions, not static constants or fully-mocked logic.

Add hand-rolled property-style tests (no proptest crate): write loops over pseudo-random or systematically generated inputs (using std, e.g. a simple LCG or fixed seed table) to assert invariants such as: serialize->deserialize round-trips an ExecutionEvent to an equal value; redaction is idempotent; filter inclusion/exclusion is consistent; the pipeline never panics on generated event streams. Keep runs deterministic and fast.

Add integration tests: extend xplainit-core/tests and xplainit-cli/tests to cover realistic end-to-end flows (load a trace JSON -> analyze/report -> assert output; dashboard analysis functions over a representative event set). Reuse the fixture/style patterns already in xplainit-core/tests/integration_tests.rs and xplainit-cli/tests/cli.rs.

Add an in-process load test (feasible offline; the plan's '1M events/sec, 10K concurrent, multi-hour' is not literally run here): feed a large event volume (e.g. hundreds of thousands of events) through the pipeline/event_store in a #[test] or #[ignore]-gated heavy test and assert it completes without error/leak and within a sane time budget, asserting throughput stays finite and stable. Document the scaled-down nature honestly in a comment.

Document fuzzing status: since cargo-fuzz is unavailable offline, add the hand-rolled generative tests above as the substitute and note in docs/TESTING.md that cargo-fuzz-based fuzzing is blocked offline, with the exact commands to run it when tooling is available. Do not fabricate fuzz results.

Run the full gate set and the four Python suites; ensure the new test count is meaningfully higher than the 178 baseline and all pass. Commit on the branch: `test: extensive unit/property/integration/load tests (FEAT-004)`.
acceptance_criteria: Test count is substantially higher than the 178 baseline, with 0 failures, and new tests target previously thin modules and the FEAT-001/002/003 additions.
Hand-rolled property-style tests exist (round-trip, redaction idempotence, filter consistency, pipeline no-panic) and are deterministic; no proptest/quickcheck dependency was added.
New integration tests exercise realistic load->analyze/report->assert flows in core and CLI.
An in-process load test drives a large event volume through the pipeline and asserts stable, error-free completion, with an honest comment about scaled-down scope.

docs/TESTING.md documents the coverage approach and states that tarpaulin coverage measurement and cargo-fuzz fuzzing are blocked offline, with commands to run them when available (no fabricated numbers).
Full gate set (build/test/clippy/fmt) passes and the four Python suites still pass.
Each new test fails if the specific code path it covers is reverted.
verification: cargo test -- --ignored  (run any heavy/load tests gated behind --ignored, if used)

source .venv/bin/activate && python test_automatic_tracing.py && cd xplainit-python && maturin develop --release && python test_frame_filter.py && python test_depth_accounting.py && python test_decorators.py
findings:
Test count raised from 203 -> 242 passing (0 failures) plus 1 #[ignore]d heavy soak test (passes under `cargo test -- --ignored`). Added three new core test files and extended the CLI suite; created docs/TESTING.md.

New files:
- xplainit-core/tests/property_tests.rs: hand-rolled property-style tests (std-only deterministic LCG; NO proptest/quickcheck added). Invariants: ExecutionEvent JSON round-trip stability, redaction idempotence+leak-freedom, FunctionFilter include/exclude consistency, pipeline never panics + sunk<=accepted, redact_events == per-event redaction. Generated maps kept to <=1 key (multi-key HashMap JSON order is randomized) and floats are integer-valued f64 (serde shortest-float reformatting made arbitrary decimals non-round-trip-stable).
- xplainit-core/tests/edge_case_tests.rs (22 tests): empty/boundary/unicode/long-string/error-branch coverage for formatter, sink, event_store, advanced_filter, async_tracker, error_explainer, explainer.
- xplainit-core/tests/load_tests.rs: in-process load tests (200k pipeline, 250k bounded store no-leak, 4-thread concurrent store) + #[ignore]d 1M-event soak. Honest comment documents this is scaled-down, NOT the plan's literal 1M/sec-10k-concurrent-multi-hour target.
- docs/TESTING.md: documents qualitative coverage approach and states tarpaulin (coverage) and cargo-fuzz (fuzzing) are BLOCKED offline, with exact commands to run each when available. No tool output fabricated.

Code change (real leak found by property test): xplainit-core/src/events.rs ExecutionEvent::redacted() now also scrubs secrets nested inside single-value payload fields (FunctionExit.return_value, Return.value, AsyncTaskResume.resumed_with, LoopIteration.loop_var_value, TypeError.value, DivisionByZero.numerator) via redacted_nested. Previously a secret object nested in a return value leaked. Added two revert-sensitive unit tests in events.rs for this.

Extended xplainit-cli/tests/cli.rs with text/markdown rendering, end-to-end secret redaction in report output, clean-trace analyze, malformed-JSON and empty-path rejection.

Gate set all green: cargo build --release, cargo test (242 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored), cargo test -- --ignored (1 passed), cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings (clean), cargo fmt --all --check (clean). Python suites all green: test_automatic_tracing 3/3, test_frame_filter 11/11, test_depth_accounting 23/23, test_decorators passing (after maturin develop --release). tarpaulin/cargo-fuzz confirmed unavailable offline; not run, documented in docs/TESTING.md.
